analysis.title: GS Basics: Bond Stability. AI Compute Bottlenecks. Frontier Model Race (Privorotsky, 12 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Rates found stability after a tumultuous week: Treasury auctions were relatively well absorbed, and longer-dated bond vols retraced about 30% of their recent move. Gold is trying to find a local low and oil is backing off the highs.

Korea sold off sharply: Kospi -3-4%, Samsung and Hynix about -4%, Taiwan broadly flat. Memory is the epicenter. CXMT announced a new 4F² DRAM architecture over the weekend, and China already has about 10% DRAM revenue share and is adding capacity, which adds to peak memory earnings concerns despite strong near-term fundamentals.

Energy: Riyadh airport was struck by Houthi missiles with no confirmed material production impact. Trump announced a Russia/Ukraine energy ceasefire, though attacks have continued, and Russian diesel is returning to the market. Brent is about $103. The author sees neither development as durable or material, but both help sentiment.

Sentiment is subdued: vol flat, fear and greed back to neutral, GS risk appetite at -1.3. Prime brokerage data shows hedge funds rotated heavily into tech but aggregate net exposure remains severely diminished. Fundamental L/S net is 52.9% (6th percentile over 1 year), even though the S&P is within an eyelash of highs.

US hedge funds rotated into Industrials and out of Info Tech, a reversal of the September trend. Info Tech was by far the most net sold sector this week at -1.0 SD after being the most-bought sector in 4 of the prior 5 weeks, with selling most pronounced Thursday on the OpenAI revenue headline.

AI compute: Google is reportedly testing Carbon, potentially competitive with Opus 5.5, and Polymarket prices Google as a serious contender for best model at end of 2026. OpenAI and Anthropic have new models not yet revealed. The OpenAI ARR volatility last week appears largely a question of accounting definitions.

The author's view is that compute remains scarce and its owners are the biggest beneficiaries. Scarcity persists partly because the market doubts the Street's ability to bring power and data center capacity online, hence the de-rating in data center supply chain names. Hyperscalers can command premium economics, and ownership of powered compute is a more durable advantage than model leadership, which can change quarterly.

Consumer: Michigan current conditions are at an all-time low. Higher rates, oil and soft real wages are hitting affordability at once. Consumption is slowing, not collapsing, and the divergence between sentiment and activity remains extraordinary.

Europe: an EU/China hybrid agreement targets about a 50% reduction in projected Chinese hybrid imports, a potential positive for European autos and a catalyst for a momentum unwind. With stability in OATs and perceived Russia/Ukraine progress, Europe looks under-owned.

Week ahead: CPI Wednesday is the main event (consensus 0.6% headline, 0.2% core), and a 10bp downside surprise on core would be meaningful for rates. Banks report from Tuesday, ASML Wednesday, TSMC Thursday, plus PPI, retail sales, and Warsh on Friday.

Positioning: speculators are heavily short bonds and the Russell and long Nasdaq, which the author sees as where the pain trade lies. The author could see headline indices tread water while under-owned Europe and the Russell outperform, and expects chop at the highs and consolidation.

Nominal growth remains very strong and fiscal spending is very high, so nominal demand keeps being generated until bonds force a stop. The author's concerns about capital intensity and crowding out will play out over time but do not matter today.

earnings_insights: Samsung's preliminary numbers 'failed to massively surpass expectations' (reported before 12 Oct 2026), a factor in the Korea memory selloff.

Upcoming: banks report from Tuesday 13 Oct, ASML Wednesday 14 Oct, TSMC Thursday 15 Oct. The author says TSMC and banks are 'already materially de-rated' and that ASML is reportedly raising spare parts prices 10%.

tension_points.bull_case: Bond vol compresses, yields stay high but stabilize, and the negative impulse on the rest of the economy relaxes. Nominal growth and fiscal spending are very strong, earnings could be supportive with AI profits compounding, and TSMC and banks are already de-rated.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy is unresolved, consumer affordability is deteriorating (Michigan current conditions at an all-time low), and capital intensity and crowding out will play out over time. The author expects chop at the highs and consolidation rather than a breakout.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 10bp downside surprise on core CPI on Wednesday would be meaningful for rates, and bonds not behaving would stop the micro from reasserting itself.
